questions.question: Explain the legal control of misleading claims on food packages. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the legal control of misleading claims on food packages.
  • Legal control of misleading claims on food packages is essential to protect consumers from false
  • or deceptive information. Regulatory authorities such as food safety agencies establish strict
  • guidelines for labeling and advertising. These laws ensure that claims related to nutrition, health
  • benefits, ingredients, and quality are scientifically valid and clearly stated. Misleading terms like
  • “natural,” “organic,” or “low-fat” must meet specific criteria before being used. Labels must not
  • exaggerate benefits or hide important information such as allergens. Violations can result in
  • penalties, product recalls, or legal action. Such regulations help maintain transparency, build
  • consumer trust, and promote fair competition in the food industry.

questions.question: Outline why amber and green glass are preferred for packaging light-sensitive food and beverage products. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline why amber and green glass are preferred for packaging light-sensitive food and
  • beverage products.
  • Amber and green glass are commonly used for packaging light -sensitive food and beverages
  • because they provide protection against harmful ultraviolet (UV) and visible light. Exposure to
  • light can cause chemical changes in food products, lead ing to spoilage, loss of flavor, color
  • degradation, and nutrient destruction. Amber glass offers the highest level of protection by
  • blocking a significant portion of UV radiation, making it suitable for products like beer and
  • certain oils. Green glass also provides moderate protection and is often used for beverages. By
  • reducing light exposure, these colored glasses help maintain product quality, extend shelf life,
  • and preserve sensory characteristics.

questions.question: Write a short note on biodegradable plastics. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a short note on biodegradable plastics.
  • Biodegradable plastics are materials that can be broken down by microorganisms such as
  • bacteria and fungi into natural substances like water, carbon dioxide, and biomass. These plastics
  • are often made from renewable resources such as starch, cellulose, or polyl actic acid (PLA).
  • They are considered environmentally friendly alternatives to conventional plastics, as they
  • reduce pollution and landfill accumulation. In food packaging, biodegradable plastics are used
  • for trays, films, and containers. However, their ef fectiveness depends on proper disposal
  • conditions, such as industrial composting facilities. While they offer sustainability benefits,
  • challenges such as cost, durability, and limited shelf life still exist.

questions.question: Discuss the role of tensile strength in handling and transportation of packaged foods. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of tensile strength in handling and transportation of packaged foods.
  • Tensile strength refers to the ability of a packaging material to withstand pulling or stretching
  • forces without breaking. It plays a crucial role in the handling and transportation of packaged
  • foods, as packages are often subjected to stress during loading, unloading, and transit. Materials
  • with high tensile strength can resist tearing and damage, ensuring that the product remains
  • protected. This property is especially important for flexible packaging such as plas tic films and
  • bags. Adequate tensile strength reduces the risk of package failure, product loss, and
  • contamination. It also contributes to maintaining the integrity and safety of food products
  • throughout the supply chain.

questions.question: Describe tin-free steel (TFS) and mention its advantages over tinplate. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe tin-free steel (TFS) and mention its advantages over tinplate.
  • Tin-free steel (TFS), also known as electrolytic chromium -coated steel, is a type of steel sheet
  • coated with chromium instead of tin. It is widely used in food packaging, especially for making
  • cans and lids. TFS pr ovides a smooth and attractive surface suitable for printing and coating.
  • One of its main advantages over tinplate is its lower cost, as it does not use expensive tin. It also
  • offers better resistance to corrosion and improved lacquer adhesion. However, un like tinplate,
  • TFS cannot be easily soldered and is usually welded. Overall, it is a cost -effective and efficient
  • alternative for certain packaging applications.

• Distinguish vibration and compression test used during transportation.
  • Vibration and compr ession tests are important methods used to evaluate the strength and
  • durability of packaging during transportation. The vibration test simulates the conditions
  • experienced during transit, such as movement and shaking, to assess how the package and its
  • contents respond to continuous motion. It helps identify potential damage caused by loosening,
  • shifting, or fatigue. On the other hand, the compression test measures the ability of a package to
  • withstand stacking loads and external pressure. It evaluates the s trength of packaging when
  • multiple units are stacked during storage or transport. While vibration testing focuses on
  • dynamic forces, compression testing deals with static load-bearing capacity.

questions.question: Describe the pouches used in food packaging. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the pouches used in food packaging.
  • Pouches are f lexible packaging solutions widely used in the food industry due to their
  • convenience, lightweight nature, and cost-effectiveness. They are made from laminated materials
  • such as plastic, aluminum foil, and paper, providing good barrier properties against m oisture,
  • oxygen, and light. Common types include stand -up pouches, flat pouches, retort pouches, and
  • spouted pouches. These pouches are used for packaging snacks, beverages, ready -to-eat meals,
  • and sauces. They are easy to handle, require less storage space, and often come with features like
  • resealable zippers. Pouches enhance product shelf life while offering attractive presentation and
  • consumer convenience.

questions.question: Write a note on types of form - fill- seal packaging machines. / [CO3] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on types of form-fill-seal packaging machines.
  • Form-fill-seal (FFS) packaging machines are automated systems used to form packages, fill them
  • with products, and seal them in a continuous process. There are mainly two types: vertical form -
  • fill-seal (VFFS) and horizontal form -fill-seal (HFFS) machines. VFFS machines form packages
  • vertically and are commonly used for powders, grains, and snack foods. HFFS machines operate
  • horizontally and are suitable for solid or semi -solid products such as biscuits and chocolates.
  • These machines improve efficiency, reduce labor costs, and ensure uniform p ackaging. They
  • also maintain hygiene and are widely used in large-scale food processing industries.

questions.question: Explain bursting strength of packaging materials. Discuss on factors affecting and its importance in food packaging applications. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain bursting strength of packaging materials. Discuss the factors affecting it and its
  • importance in food packaging applications.
  • Bursting strength is the ability of a packaging material, particularly paper and paperboard, to
  • withstand internal pressure before it ruptures. It is measured using instruments like the Mullen
  • tester, where pressure is applied until the material bursts. This property is crucial in determining
  • the durability and resistance of packaging during handling, storage, and transportation. Several
  • factors affect bursting strength, including the type and quality of raw ma terials, fiber length,
  • bonding between fibers, thickness of the material, and moisture content. Higher moisture levels
  • can weaken the structure, reducing strength. Manufacturing processes such as refining and
  • pressing also influence fiber bonding and overall strength. The importance of bursting strength in
  • food packaging lies in its ability to protect products from mechanical damage and external
  • pressure. Strong packaging prevents leakage, contamination, and spoilage, ensuring product
  • safety and maintaining quality throughout the supply chain.

questions.question: Describe the manufacture of paper for packaging purpose and discuss how processing affects its properties. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the manufacture of paper for packaging purpose and discuss how processing affects
  • its properties.
  • The manufacture of paper for packaging involves several key steps, starting with the selection of
  • raw materials such as wood pulp, recycled paper, or other fibrous materials. The process begins
  • with pulping, where raw materials are broken down into fibers through mechanical or chemical
  • methods. The pulp is then cleaned, screened, and sometimes bleached to impro ve quality. Next,
  • the pulp is formed into sheets on a wire mesh, where water is drained, and fibers interlock to
  • form a continuous web. This sheet is then pressed and dried to remove remaining moisture.
  • Additional treatments such as coating, sizing, and ca lendaring may be applied to enhance
  • properties. Processing conditions significantly affect paper properties such as strength, thickness,
  • smoothness, porosity, and printability. For example, increased refining improves fiber bonding
  • and strength, while exce ssive drying may reduce flexibility. Coating enhances barrier properties
  • and appearance. Thus, careful control of processing parameters is essential to produce paper
  • suitable for specific packaging applications.

questions.question: Outline the protective, containment, and communication functions of food packaging in the food industry / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the protective, containment, and communication functions of food packaging in the
  • food industry.
  • Food packaging performs three major functions: protection, containment, and communication.
  • The protective function involves safeguarding food from physical, chemical, and biological
  • hazards such as moisture, oxygen, light, microorganisms, and mechanical damage. This helps in
  • preserving quality, extending shelf life, and ensuring food safety. The containment function
  • refers to holding the product in a convenient form for handling, storage, and transportation. It
  • prevents leakage, spillage, and loss of product, making distribution efficient. The communication
  • function provides essential information to consumers through labeling, including ingredients,
  • nutritional facts, expiry date, usage instruc tions, and safety warnings. It also plays a role in
  • marketing by attracting consumers through design and branding. Together, these functions
  • ensure that food reaches consumers in a safe, convenient, and informative manner, supporting
  • both industry operations and consumer needs.

questions.question: Describe paper types,uses and its applications. / [CO2] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe paper types, uses, and its applications.
  • Paper used in food packaging is available in various types, each designed for specific
  • applications based on its properties. Common types include kraft paper, greaseproof paper,
  • glassine paper, parchment paper, and paperboard. Kraft paper is strong and durable, widely used
  • for bags and wrapping materials. Greaseproof paper resists oil and is used for packaging fatty
  • foods like butter and bakery products. Glassine paper is smooth an d translucent, often used for
  • wrapping confectionery items. Parchment paper provides resistance to moisture and grease,
  • making it suitable for baking and food wrapping. Paperboard, including corrugated board, is used
  • for cartons, boxes, and bulk packaging. These materials are used in a wide range of applications
  • such as food wrapping, takeaway containers, beverage cartons, and shipping boxes. Paper
  • packaging is biodegradable, recyclable, and cost-effective, making it an environmentally friendly
  • choice. Its versatility and adaptability make it an essential material in the food packaging
  • industry.
